children: Disney's (ESPN) has reportedly worked out a new six-year contract with Joe Buck with worth approximately $108M. The contract extension will keep Buck as the voice of "Monday Night Football" and key playoff games through 2031. Buck was in the final season of his previous five-year deal. His 25-year broadcast partner, Troy Aikman, has not signed a new deal yet.
Sources indicated that Buck's annual salary will increase to $18M from $15M.

Joe Buck began broadcasting in 1989 while attending Indiana University, calling Triple-A Louisville Redbirds games. In 1991, he joined his father, legendary announcer Jack Buck, on St. Louis Cardinals radio and television broadcasts. Fox Sports

hired Buck in 1994 for NFL coverage, and he soon became one of the network sports’ leading voices. At 27, he called the 1996 World Series, becoming the youngest television play-by-play announcer to do so since Vin Scully. He later led FOX’s MLB and NFL coverage, calling six Super Bowls and more than two decades of World Series broadcasts. In 2022, Buck and longtime partner Troy Aikman moved to ESPN/ABC to become the lead team for Monday Night Football.

title: ESPN extends lead NFL announcer Joe Buck for 6 years
